sources.title: Articles on Smashing Magazine — For Web Designers And Developers

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Vitaly Friedman)
articles.description: Many companies assume everyone craves new AI features. But the reality is that most people don't want more AI — at least not in the way most AI leaders envision it. Brought to you by Design Patterns For AI Interfaces, **friendly video courses on UX** and design patterns by Vitaly.
articles.title: No, People Don’t Want More AI In Their Life

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Anastasia Sycheva)
articles.description: The strongest visual concepts don’t start in Figma. They start with the right questions. Explore the pre-concept phase of brand identity design, where teams research brand context, uncover hidden assumptions with stakeholders, and turn shared direction into a visual foundation before a single concept is created.
articles.title: From Kickoff To First Concept: How To Turn Brand Strategy Into Visual Direction

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Kat Homan)
articles.description: Many UI trends are designed to capture attention and signal innovation, but those goals often conflict with the needs of mental health apps: reducing cognitive strain, fostering trust, and providing a sense of refuge. Kat Homan introduces an evaluation framework that helps designers assess whether trendy visual and interaction patterns support or undermine the unique goals of mental health experiences.
articles.title: Designing For Distressed Users: Why Mental Health Apps Shouldn’t Follow Every UI Fashion

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Zareen Tasnim)
articles.description: We have been building websites inside boxes for years on WordPress. Let’s take a closer look at [Kirki](https://kirki.com/), the first freeform visual builder with an infinite canvas, and explore how it redefines the experience with cleaner performance, full design freedom, and zero plugin dependency.
articles.title: Meet Kirki: WordPress’s First Visual Builder With An Infinite Canvas

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Vitaly Friedman)
articles.description: A closer look at why users don’t need more tools in their daily lives. What they need are seamless integrations of useful features to match already existing, established mental models. Brought to you by Design Patterns For AI Interfaces, **friendly video course on UX** and design patterns by Vitaly.
articles.title: Users Don’t Need More Tools: They Need Seamless Integrations

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Victor Yocco)
articles.description: We’ve fallen into conversational tunnel vision, defaulting every AI capability into a chat-based interface simply because LLMs are trained on dialogue data. But great UX is about matching modality to users’ context, intent, and cognitive load, so the interface adapts to the user, not the other way around.
articles.title: Matching AI Modality To User Intent: Designing The Right Interface

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Mikhail Prosmitskiy)
articles.description: Teams can generate UI faster than ever, but they still have to guarantee that what they ship is usable, secure, and maintainable. Accessibility as an operational capability rather than a compliance checklist or end-of-project audit, and what that looks like in practice.
articles.title: Why Accessibility Is An Operational Capability, Not A Feature

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Cosima Mielke)
articles.description: July is just around the corner, and that means... It’s time for some new desktop wallpapers! As every month, the wallpapers in this collection were created by the community for the community and can be downloaded for free. Enjoy!
articles.title: Snapshots Of Summer (July 2026 Wallpapers Edition)
